name: svg-draw-on-scroll

frames.best_why: Route is nearly complete with all four stop labels and the pink tip marker in view.

tagline: Winding route draws itself as you scroll, a pink dot on its tip.
summary: A single curvy line that draws itself from start to finish as its container scrolls, with a glowing dot riding the growing tip and small tags pinned beside the route.
appearance: On black, a thin white line snakes down through four broad curves to the bottom. Four small rounded tags label the stops, and a bright pink dot with a soft halo sits on the stroke's current end.
behaviour: Scrolling longerens the stroke from the top while the dot tracks its tip and the stop tags hold their places. Scrolling back shortens the line again unless the run-once option freezes it fully drawn.
demo_content: Dolomites day-three hike with stops at Lake Sorapis and Forcella Marcuoira plus distance stats.
search_phrases: line that draws itself on scroll
animated trail map for a journey
route illustration that reveals on scroll
story map with pinned stop labels
progressive line reveal on page scroll
path grows from top as you read
use_when: A trip, timeline or process page wants a route to unfold in step with the reader's scrolling.
avoid_when: It needs a scrollable ancestor and a tall sized box, and the drawing is hidden from assistive tech.
customise: Path data, an optional set of paths, viewBox, stroke colour and width, scroll offset, run-once, the marker node and the scroll container are all props.
weight_why: One stroke and one marker following a spring while scrolling; still when parked.

a11y.note: The SVGs are aria-hidden, so the route and its stops have no accessible description beyond the text tags.

issues: The heading and scroll hint scroll out of view by frame 3, so later frames lose the intro copy.
The stop tags are placed by the demo with fixed percentages, so they can drift off the drawn line.
polish_why: Tight scroll-linked draw with a marker on the stroke; hand-placed labels can slip.
